what_its_for: Cabergoline is used to treat conditions caused by too much prolactin hormone in your body (called hyperprolactinemia). High prolactin can cause irregular periods, unwanted breast milk production, fertility problems, and certain types of pituitary gland tumors (called prolactinomas). It works by acting on the brain to reduce the amount of prolactin your body makes.
how_to_take: Take cabergoline by mouth with or without food. Taking it with food may help if you feel nauseous. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. It is usually taken only TWICE a week (for example, Monday and Thursday), not every day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose, usually 0.25 mg (one-quarter of a 1 mg tablet or half of a 0.5 mg tablet) twice a week. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over several weeks or months depending on your prolactin levels and how you respond to treatment. The usual maintenance dose is 0.25 mg to 1 mg taken twice a week. Never change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and remember the SAME DAY, take it as soon as you remember. If you do not remember until the NEXT DAY, skip the missed dose entirely and take your next scheduled dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses on the same day or double up to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store cabergoline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking cabergoline, as it can increase dizziness and other side effects. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require full alertness until you know how this medication affects you, because it can cause dizziness, fainting, or sudden sleepiness. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medication can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because some medications (such as antipsychotics and certain blood pressure drugs) can interact with cabergoline.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden chest pain, shortness of breath, or difficulty breathing (possible signs of heart or lung problems); uncontrollable urges such as gambling, increased sexual urges, overeating, or compulsive spending (impulse control problems); severe stomach or back pain; sudden confusion, vision changes, or unusual weakness; hallucinations or severe mood changes; or swelling of the legs or feet. Call your doctor if you experience ongoing nausea, vomiting, or dizziness; unusual tiredness; headaches that do not go away; or if you think you may be pregnant while on this medication.
when_it_works: Cabergoline usually begins to lower prolactin levels within the first 2 to 4 weeks of treatment. Many people notice improvements in symptoms such as irregular periods or unwanted milk production within a few weeks to a couple of months. If you are being treated for a prolactinoma (pituitary tumor), it may take several months to see a reduction in tumor size. Keep taking your medication even if you feel well. Your doctor will check your prolactin levels with regular blood tests to make sure the medication is working properly.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Cabergoline is generally stopped once pregnancy is confirmed. Discuss your treatment plan with your doctor before trying to conceive. BREASTFEEDING: Do not use cabergoline if you are breastfeeding, as it stops milk production. OLDER ADULTS: Use with caution as older adults may be more sensitive to dizziness and falls. LIVER PROBLEMS: If you have significant liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. HEART CONDITIONS: Tell your doctor if you have any history of heart valve problems or lung scarring (fibrosis), as cabergoline may worsen these conditions with long-term use.
